raw_response:
I am 67 years old and I have been farming these fields in Quzhou for more than 50 years. My family has about 9 mu of land, and I know every inch of it. At my age, I do not have the strength to chase after newfangled crops or take big risks, so I stick to what has always put food on the table and money in my pocket.

This year, just like last year, I will plant winter wheat on 7 mu of my best land. I will sow *Jimai 22* — it is an improved variety that my neighbors and I have used for years, and it gives me a steady yield of about 1,000 jin per mu. Before sowing in October, I do rotary tillage to break up the soil and bury the maize stubble properly. I put down compound fertilizer as basal dressing — about 100 jin per mu — and top-dress with urea in the spring when the wheat turns green. All together that comes to about 20 jin of nitrogen per mu, plus 11 jin of phosphate and 5 jin of potash. Wheat is thirsty, so I irrigate four times: before winter, at green-up, at jointing, and at grain filling. I spray three or four times for aphids and weeds.

After I cut the wheat in early June, I will plant *Denghai 605* hybrid maize on those same 7 mu. I use no-tillage — I just drill the seed straight into the wheat stubble. It saves diesel, saves my back, and the yield is good, about 1,150 jin per mu. Maize does not need as much nitrogen as wheat — about 12 jin per mu from compound fertilizer is enough, plus 3 jin of phosphate and 3 jin of potash. I irrigate twice in the summer if the rains are short, and spray two or three times for corn borers and weeds.

I have also kept 2 mu for cotton. I know it is hard work with all the spraying, but the cotton price has been steady and my neighbor helps me pick it at harvest. I grow a hybrid cotton variety, rotary till the plot in spring, and apply compound fertilizer with a bit more phosphorus and potassium — about 9 jin of nitrogen, 8 jin of phosphate, and 7.5 jin of potash per mu. I irrigate twice and spray about 15 times through the season to keep the bollworms away. I expect about 500 jin of seed cotton per mu.

That is my plan: wheat-maize double cropping on 7 mu, cotton on 2 mu. It is what I know, and at my age, that is the safest bet.
